{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "For Success (binary outcome), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than ANOVA",
    "Given the large sample size (n=76655), check for violations of normality and homoscedasticity; consider Welch's ANOVA if variance heterogeneity is severe",
    "Include Mouse as a random effect or blocking factor in a mixed-effects model to account for the 8 mice contributing repeated measures"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For significant ANOVA results, perform pairwise comparisons between all 10 pairs of stimulation paradigms using Tukey's HSD for continuous variables",
    "For Success (binary), use pairwise chi-square tests with Bonferroni correction or logistic regression with post-hoc odds ratio comparisons",
    "Focus comparisons on Sham versus active stimulation conditions, and Combined versus unimodal conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only)",
    "Report effect sizes (Cohen's d for continuous variables, Cramer's V or odds ratios for Success) alongside p-values"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Bonferroni correction across the 5 response variables and 10 pairwise comparisons per variable (50 tests total), or alternatively control FDR at 0.05 using Benjamini-Hochberg procedure given the large number of tests; for Tukey's HSD, family-wise error rate is controlled within each response variable",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression is recommended as the primary predictive model because Stim Paradigm is a 5-level categorical response without natural ordering. This models the log-odds of each stimulation paradigm relative to a reference category (e.g., Sham) as a function of the five performance variables. Alternative: Random forest or gradient boosting for non-linear relationships and variable interactions, with cross-validation to assess classification accuracy. Given the class imbalance (Combined: 48846, Sham: 3505), use stratified sampling and report balanced accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 per class rather than overall accuracy.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Check normality of residuals for each continuous variable using Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on subsamples due to large n",
    "Assess homogeneity of variances using Levene's test; apply Welch's ANOVA or transform variables if violated",
    "For multinomial logistic regression: verify independence of irrelevant alternatives (IIA) assumption using Hausman-McFadden test",
    "Check for multicollinearity among predictors (VIF < 5); Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target may be correlated",
    "Examine for influential observations and outliers given extreme max values (e.g., Time-to-Target max=201.39, Path Efficiency max=29.82)",
    "Verify that Mouse effects are adequately modeled via random effects or fixed effects adjustment"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham will show significantly lower Success (0.27 vs 0.67-0.78), higher Time-to-Target (4.68s vs 2.56-3.14s), lower Path Efficiency (0.31 vs 0.43-0.50), lower Average Speed (10.74 vs 11.97-12.83), and lower AD (0.24 vs 0.34-0.40) compared to all active stimulation paradigms",
    "Combined stimulation will show optimal or near-optimal performance across metrics, potentially outperforming unimodal conditions",
    "Bright Visual Only may outperform Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only on Success and Time-to-Target based on marginal means",
    "AD (angular dispersion) will likely discriminate Sham from active conditions, with higher values indicating more exploratory/search behavior in stimulated mice",
    "Multinomial logistic regression will achieve moderate-to-high classification accuracy, with best discrimination for Sham vs. Combined, and potential confusion among unimodal visual/ICMS conditions"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe class imbalance in Stim Paradigm (Combined: 63.7% of data, Sham: 4.6%) will bias predictive models toward majority class and reduce statistical power for minority classes",
    "Cross-sectional summary data obscures trial-level structure and temporal dynamics; cannot assess learning effects or session-level variability",
    "Mouse-level clustering (8 mice) introduces non-independence not fully addressable without raw trial-level data with mouse identifiers",
    "Extreme outliers in Path Efficiency (max=29.82) and Time-to-Target (max=201.39) suggest data quality issues or failed trials that may require censoring",
    "No information on trial order, session structure, or experimental design (e.g., blocked vs. interleaved) limits causal inference",
    "Temperature=0.0 in LLM generation may produce overconfident but potentially less calibrated uncertainty estimates if this were an LLM-based analysis"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression with Mouse as random intercept, using the five performance variables as fixed effects, and evaluate predictive performance via stratified 10-fold cross-validation. Additionally, conduct a multivariate MANOVA to test for overall stimulation paradigm effects across all five response variables simultaneously, followed by discriminant function analysis to identify which linear combinations of performance variables best separate the five paradigms. Finally, explore non-linear predictive models (random forest, XGBoost) with hyperparameter tuning to establish a performance ceiling for paradigm classification."
}
